AirTag is a great way to protect and track your luggage, but attaching one to smaller items like a camera can be challenging.

Some people simply toss an AirTag into a generic case and clip it to a camera strap, but that's hardly discreet—a thief can easily spot it and toss it away. Fortunately, there are better ways…

Apple has always stressed that AirTag is not primarily an anti-theft device. Its anti-stalking features mean a thief will eventually be notified that an AirTag is present. However, you have a few hours before that notification kicks in to track your gear, so plenty of people use it for this purpose.

Of course, if a thief spots and discards the AirTag quickly, that tracking window disappears. That's why a regular case—though cheap and easy to attach—often makes the tracker too easy to spot.

Fortunately, there are more discreet ways to attach an AirTag to a DSLR or mirrorless camera.

Camera strap clips

The most basic method is to use a camera strap clip. These accessories blend right in with the strap itself, and they're even less noticeable if you use a black camera strap—especially a thick, comfort-style one.

Quick-release plates

Many photographers keep a tripod quick-release plate permanently attached to the bottom of their camera for convenience. You can buy plates that include a built-in AirTag slot, making it far less conspicuous.

Tripod adapters

If it's hard to find a quick-release plate compatible with your tripod, another option is to use a universal adapter.

Camera cages

If you use a camera cage to mount accessories, you can either buy one with a built-in AirTag slot or add a dedicated cage accessory with a slot. The latter isn't discreet on its own, but when mounted on a cage full of gear, it usually blends right in.

L-brackets

The newest accessory is Peak Design's Field Bracket. It's an L-bracket that lets you mount your camera horizontally or vertically on a tripod, and it has extras like a hand strap mount and a multi-hole baseplate to expand your kit. However, it doesn't use an AirTag—instead, it has a built-in tracker compatible with Find My.

Have you tried any of these methods, or do you have another clever trick? Share it in the comments.
